cards.text: Last time, Delilah got Samson's secret, his hair was shaved, and the Philistines gouged out his eyes and put him to grinding grain in a Gaza prison. But his hair started growing back. Now the lords of the Philistines gather to offer a great sacrifice to their god Dagon.

cards.question: The lords of the Philistines are celebrating at the sacrifice to Dagon. What do they say their god did for them?

answers.text: Sent rain down on their fields

cards.question: When the people see Samson, they praise their god and call Samson the enemy who destroyed their land and multiplied their dead.

cards.text: The party's rolling, and their hearts are merry. Friend, I've been to enough office parties to know that when a room gets THIS happy, somebody's about to have an idea.

cards.question: They call for Samson. So they bring him out of the prison to ___ them.
Samson's out of the prison and in front of the crowd. Where do the Philistines station him?

cards.text: Samson can't see a thing, so a servant is holding his hand. Then Samson speaks up and asks the servant for something.

cards.question: Samson tells the servant, "Lead me where I can feel the ___ supporting the temple, so I can lean against them."

cards.text: This temple is PACKED: all the lords of the Philistines, and about three thousand men and women up on the roof alone, watching Samson. And I thought the junk drawer was crowded.
Then Samson calls out to the LORD: "O Lord GOD, please remember me." Friend, after all my years in the back of a junk drawer, I KNOW that prayer.

cards.question: In his prayer, Samson asks God to strengthen him just once more.
Samson asks for one blow to pay the Philistines back for his two ___.

cards.text: Samson reaches out for the two central pillars holding up the temple. Right hand on one, left hand on the other.

cards.question: Samson is braced between the two central pillars of the temple. What does he say?

answers.text: Let me die with the Philistines
Let me go free from this place
Let me rest here for a while

cards.question: Then Samson pushes on the pillars with all his might. What happens to the temple?

answers.text: It falls on the lords and all the people
Only the roof comes crashing down

cards.question: In his death, Samson killed fewer than he had killed in his life.

cards.text: Afterward, Samson's brothers and his father's family come down to get him, and they carry him back.

cards.question: Samson's family carries him back. Where do they bury him?
One last detail about Samson: he had judged Israel for ___ years.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 8 quotes "Lead me where I can feel the ___ supporting the temple, so I can lean against them.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card retells events from the previous passage: Delilah getting the secret, the shaving, the gouged eyes, grinding in the Gaza prison and the hair growing back (Judges 16:17-22). The card cites only Judges 16:23, so those Bible facts have no reference.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: "After all my years in the back of a junk drawer, I KNOW that prayer" implies Papa Dorin prayed to the Lord in the drawer. His backstory has him not knowing who the Most High was until the angel came ("The most… who?"), so the line adds something new to his story and contradicts it. It could be reworded as knowing what it's like to want to be remembered.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The opening card begins "Last time," which assumes the baker played the previous passage in the Samson group. Papa Dorin isn't told how the baker has done before, but these passages run in a story group.
findings.question: Can Papa Dorin refer to the previous passage in a story group as "last time," or should the opening card give the context without assuming the baker has played it?
